strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal cross-platform VPN whose logical weak-network behavior approaches UDP/QUIC while public carriers remain stock REALITY/Vision over real kernel TCP.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: M10-002 pinned QUIC oracle integration and broader seeded weak-network profiles
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not tune RBC/FEC policy, freeze a production FEC frame, modify REALITY/Vision, or start TUN/platform integration until a locally executed pinned QUIC stream/datagram oracle is compared with the M10 deterministic/native-socket baselines. Keep the main WBD module on its current toolchain unless a dedicated toolchain ADR and regression gate explicitly changes it.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Completed M10-001 at substantive HEAD 1f2b11424d6eeac8f8d092a236872f48e49c5799: added a versioned deterministic benchmark/report layer with six fixed profiles and 60 strategy/multiplier results, a runnable cmd/wbd-bench JSON report, real 127.0.0.1 tcp4/udp4 fault-proxy smoke tests, bounded soft-deadline tail-recovery candidate, same-XOR-pair counterexample, and a machine-readable QUIC oracle pin. The real socket smoke showed one 35 ms serial TCP stall holding later records to roughly 38-40 ms while later UDP datagrams still arrived around 1-2 ms. The deterministic single-stall profile gives native TCP p95=80 ms, WBD 1.5x reinjection p95=20 ms and 1.5x XOR/duplicate p95=10 ms, while the same-XOR-pair burst keeps XOR at 80 ms and reinjection at 20 ms. Final-chunk GAP-only completion remains 80 ms; the bounded soft-deadline candidate reduces it to 50 ms. quic-go is pinned at v0.61.0 / 579ee19 and requires Go 1.25.0, so it is not silently linked into the current Go 1.23 module. Local vet, normal/race tests, protocol fuzz (~132k executions), Linux/386, Linux/mipsle and Windows/amd64 benchmark cross-builds, CLI cross-builds, handoff verification and continuity tests passed; remote CI and handoff-verify also passed.
continuation_cursor.current_task: M10-002: locally execute the pinned quic-go v0.61.0 oracle in an isolated compatible Go toolchain, add QUIC stream and datagram rows to the benchmark report without upgrading the WBD module by accident, and broaden deterministic profiles with seeded jitter/loss distributions after the oracle baseline is stable.
continuation_cursor.why_now: M10-001 now separates reproducible model statistics from real kernel socket semantics and has a quantified TCP/UDP/WBD baseline. QUIC is the missing reliable-stream/datagram oracle needed before choosing RBC allocation, FEC shape, or tail timer policy.
continuation_cursor.done_when: A pinned quic-go v0.61.0 oracle is built and run inside the local sandbox with a recorded compatible Go toolchain, produces repeatable stream and datagram benchmark rows comparable to native TCP/UDP and WBD candidates, the oracle identity/toolchain hashes are recorded without committing binaries, and at least one seeded jitter/loss profile family is added with stable report output. If the local environment cannot qualify the oracle, record the exact blocker and do not substitute Actions PASS as local qualification.
